title: TraceQA replay result
description: replay.json, written by `traceqa replay` into its run folder (feature replay) next to run.json and events.jsonl: for each edge of a graph.json that was asked for, whether performing it again led where it did. Given the same site and graph the file is byte-identical: keys are sorted, the steps are in the order asked for, and nothing in it is a time. A component is found again by its id, and a page is the screen the graph says by the rule the walk used (the share of the same component ids, `stateSimilarityPerMille`), built from the graph itself.

mode.description: chain: edges that follow one another from the start page, done in one session, and ended at the first that does not lead where it did. all: every edge of the graph, each from the screen it was made on.

ended.description: Why the replay ended. complete: every edge asked for was dealt with. timeout and max-requests: that limit was reached, and the edges not reached are not-run. cancelled: Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. error: the browser failed; the message is in events.jsonl.

actions.description: How many actions were made, the ones that only reopened a screen included.

steps.description: One entry for each edge asked for, in the order asked.

schemaVersion.description: The layout version of the graph.json.

startUrl.description: The address the replay started from, with secret parameters replaced. It is the graph's own, or, with --origin, the graph's with its origin changed.

ReplayCounts.description: How the steps came out. `replayable` is the steps that were asked for and that the walk had completed: the others are recorded-failed and are not counted against the replay.

reproducedPerMille.description: reproduced out of replayable, in thousandths, rounded down. Absent when nothing was replayable.

ReplayStep.description: One edge, and what performing it again came to.

edge.description: The edge, as named in graph.json.

state.description: The screen the edge was made on.

outcome.description: reproduced: the page is the screen the graph says. diverged: the action was made, or failed, and the page is not that screen. missing: the component is not on the page, and nothing was done. blocked: the safety rules leave it alone (a replay is read-only unless --allow-writes), or there is no recorded text to type. not-run: it was not tried, because an earlier step of the chain broke, its screen could not be reopened, or the replay ended first. recorded-failed: the walk did not complete it, so there is nothing to compare with.

expected.description: The screen the edge led to in the walk. Absent for an edge that led nowhere.

actual.description: For reproduced, the same as expected. For diverged, the screen the page was, or `unknown` for a page the graph has no screen like. Absent when the action did not complete.

note.description: Why, in a sentence, when there is something to say.
